content_html:
Before writing the actual thoughts, just one comment: I am writing this at 1am of a friday at the Hyatt right above the Grand Central Station at NYC. From all the places in the world, none come closer to my childhood dream than New York, so pretty happy to be here. Now going into the actual matters

Frictionless world

Since the beginning of the beginning human have needs. Humans do stuff to satisfy those needs. Those "stuffs" require certain traits: intelligence, time, experience, social skills, a dick, whatever. Wanna buy a new i

Phone because you are a fucking retail addict? Okay. Get the fucking money (working, heritage, robery) and wait in the line for 20hr for the new release. Wanna have sex? Great. Be someone who can talk to a girl or pay here. For all goals that we have there is something in between us. Let's call it obstacles.

Some of those obstacles are actually real: IQ for quant, height for basketball, or being blind to seeing. And some of those are what I am going to call friction: waiting in line, spending xxxhr in traffic to get to one place, doing a lot of boring work to get the fucking money, etc. Basically, my definition of friction is: think of the most genetically unlucky guy you know. If he still can make the task, then it's friction.

So if every retarded can make the task, what differentiate people? Will. Wanting more than the others. That's simple. You don't need to be special to go at the "exclusive Taylor Swift show". If you want this shit so much that you're willing to spend 100 fucking hours waiting. you got it. Neither it's hard to send emails to get an answer for investment banking. You just need to spend the fucking time. Getting jacked? No problem. Just spend time at the gym.

Either way, the story is the same. Not a problem. Just want more. Wanting is the friction.

Now suppose (hypothetically obvious) that some new technology came that make the mapping from wanting -> having way faster, so that every human can achieve in a really easy way what they want. What am I talking about?

AI obviously. But also computers. And eletricity. And HVAC. And Fire. Every fucking technology we created just made this path from wanting to having easier. Since the beggining of the ages, the friction to getting what you want has been reduced. Or has it?
